transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (HarborAnalytics Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (CTO), Sara Gomez (DevOps Lead)
---
Summary:
Quick operational QBR/checkpoint to align on SLA targets, budget impact of different rollout strategies, and next steps for the pilot benchmark. Discussed hosted vs dedicated economics, VPC constraints, SOC2/audit needs, and a tentative pilot kickoff window.
Topics:
- Current usage and cost profile
- SLA targets and incident runbooks
- Model rollout plan (canary, A/B, fallback)
- Pilot benchmark scope and logistics
- Security/compliance artifacts needed
Action items and next steps captured above.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give a 50 minute-ish rundown, thanks Priya, Tom, Sara for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hey all, Priya here.
[00:14] Tom Reynolds: Tom here.
[00:16] Sara Gomez: Sara, hi.
[00:18] Liam Ortiz: Liam from Redwood.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great. Agenda: usage snapshot, SLA budgeting, model rollout options and pilot logistics. We'll try to leave 10 minutes for Qs.
[00:32] Tom Reynolds: Quick context — our production feature has about 120 qps on average for the user-facing recommender, spikes to 450 in the evening. We tightened tokenization so token counts are lower but still costy, excuse me costly.
[00:45] Priya Nair: Also want to call out quality/regression tolerance — if model swap affects latency >50ms or top-1 accuracy drops by 3%, we flag.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Good, that's helpful. On our side we looked at three paths: hosted API with burst capacity, Dedicated reserved pools with pinned GPUs, or Private (VPC) deployment. Each has different latency and unit-cost profiles.
[01:18] Liam Ortiz: I'll put numbers — for your 120/450 qps profile, hosted with our standard gpt-family-ish open model is about $X per 1M tokens, but the big lever is batching and KV prefix cache. If you have repeated prompts, caching can cut token spend by 20-40%.
[01:41] Sara Gomez: Quick question — we cannot send PII off our VPC; so Private or VPC peering is a must for the pilot. Is that doable?
[01:51] Liam Ortiz: Yes, VPC peering supported. We'll need to coordinate CIDR ranges, egress rules, and a one-time network window. We also have an on-prem packaged option but prefer to start with VPC to speed pilot.
[02:05] Priya Nair: What's the latency delta if we go VPC vs hosted?
[02:09] Liam Ortiz: Usually VPC adds ~10-30ms depending on routing. Hosted in-region is lowest but data residency matters. Our Dedicated pools are similar latency once reserved, and you can pin model variants for consistent tail latency.
[02:25] Tom Reynolds: Budget constraints — finance wants to cap this pilot to a maximum incremental $12k/month. We need clarity on runway.
[02:34] Maya Chen: Understood. We proposed two pilot pricing options in the earlier deck: cost-per-token with a reserved burst cap, or a fixed pilot commit that includes benchmark runs. We'll send a revised spreadsheet.
[02:48] Priya Nair: For the benchmark, we'd like to run two scenarios: typical daytime workload and an evening spike. Also a long-tail prompt set that stresses KV cache.
[02:58] Liam Ortiz: That's perfect. We'll script the daytime pattern and use your sample prompts. Note: if prompts are highly diverse, batching effectiveness drops and cost rises.
[03:12] Sara Gomez: Security — we need SOC 2, SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs retained for 90 days. Also, we may require HSM for keys later. Do you support that?
[03:25] Liam Ortiz: Yes to SOC 2, SSO via SAML, KMS/HSM integration available on Private, and audit logs are configurable. We'll share the SOC2 artifact and network diagram.
[03:37] Tom Reynolds: Any gotchas for network egress? Our security team blocks outbound to unknown IP ranges.
[03:43] Maya Chen: We can provide static egress IP ranges for the VPC endpoint and a whitelistable host. That's in the network doc Liam will share.
[03:55] Priya Nair: Rolling out models — we plan to test a distilled variant for cost savings. What's Redwood's recommended rollout pattern?
[04:05] Liam Ortiz: Typical pattern: canary (1-5% traffic) -> A/B (50/50) -> full rollout with automatic rollback on quality regressions. We also support automatic fallback to a cheaper model if tail latency exceeds SLO. The runtime swaps KV caches where compatible.
[04:23] Priya Nair: Does fallback mean different embedding mismatch risk?
[04:27] Liam Ortiz: There can be embedding drift; we recommend embedding anchoring and periodic re-embedding, and we can pin model versions to avoid silent drift. We'll capture that in the runbook.
[04:42] Tom Reynolds: For canary, how do you handle metrics? We need latency p95, p99, and model quality telemetry.
[04:50] Liam Ortiz: The Redwood Console exposes per-route p50/p95/p99, token costs, and model-level quality hooks. You can also send us a set of golden prompts and we can run evals automatically post-deploy.
[05:02] Sara Gomez: Are there costs for the Console retention beyond standard?
[05:06] Maya Chen: Advanced observability retention is an add-on, we can outline retention tiers and pricing in the spreadsheet.
[05:14] Priya Nair: Regarding the pilot benchmark itself, can Redwood run it in our VPC or do we run it from our infra?
[05:22] Liam Ortiz: Either works. For speed, Redwood SEs can orchestrate from a Redwood-managed test harness that executes from a peered VPC to replicate production routing. We'll provide the harness repo link and the load checklist.
[05:35] Priya Nair: Ok good. We want deterministic results so we'll share seed data and traffic traces.
[05:40] Maya Chen: Next — incident postmortem expectations. If we hit SLA breach, what do you want in the contract?
[05:47] Tom Reynolds: We need an SLO credit structure and a priority on-fix SLA for severity-1 incidents.
[05:54] Liam Ortiz: We offer SLA credits for uptime breaches in Dedicated/reserved contracts and a 4-hr on-call response for Sev-1 on Enterprise plans. We'll confirm exact language.
[06:06] Priya Nair: Any limitations on model sizes or sequence lengths that could affect p99?
[06:11] Liam Ortiz: Very long sequences can push kernel selection and increase tail latency. We can recommend quantized variants and KV windowing to mitigate. Also continuous batching policies are tunable per-route.
[06:25] Maya Chen: Let's talk timeline. If we get artifacts this week and pricing, can we aim for a pilot kickoff the week of June 8, with a 48–72 hour benchmark run?
[06:36] Priya Nair: That aligns with our internal calendar. Finance sign-off might come earlier if numbers look reasonable.
[06:44] Tom Reynolds: On the cost trade-off — show us the delta between hosted burst pricing vs Dedicated hourly amortization at our expected utilization.
[06:53] Maya Chen: We'll include a side-by-side with runrate and an example amortization showing breakeven at ~60% sustained utilization.
[07:02] Sara Gomez: For the VPC setup do you need any specific ports open?
[07:07] Liam Ortiz: HTTPS outbound and the egress IP whitelist; we'll provide the exact ports in the network doc, but mainly 443 and our healthcheck endpoints.
[07:18] Priya Nair: Questions from our security reviewers — do you perform model provenance checks or certify open models?
[07:24] Liam Ortiz: We maintain a model catalog with verified performance profiles and known provenance for curated open models; we can provide the onboarding checklist. Some models have authored provenance metadata, some require extra vetting.
[07:39] Tom Reynolds: Benchmarks — please include tail-latency percentiles, token cost per request, and relative quality delta vs our baseline.
[07:48] Liam Ortiz: Affirmative. We'll instrument the harness to emit those metrics to your Prometheus endpoint and to Redwood Console for cross-checking.
[07:58] Priya Nair: For the pilot, we want automated rollback if top-1 drop >3% on golden set or p99 > 600ms. Can Redwood automate both signals?
[08:08] Liam Ortiz: Yes, we can wire those as automated rollout guards. We recommend starting with manual approvals on the first canary then enabling auto-rollback on the second.
[08:21] Maya Chen: Any blocker from your side on security or legal?
[08:25] Tom Reynolds: Legal needs the contract redline but no blockers right now. Security wants the SOC2 docs and the static egress ranges.
[08:33] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize getting that over.
[08:36] Priya Nair: One more — if the pilot shows cost savings we may want to scope a Dedicated commit in Q3. Can you model that projection?
[08:46] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include a 6- and 12-month projection comparing hosted vs Dedicated commits including amortized GPU cost, expected unit cost with batching and cache.
[08:58] Sara Gomez: For the KV cache, if we pin model versions, does the cache persist across rollouts?
[09:03] Liam Ortiz: If model architecture is compatible, the KV cache can be reused; otherwise we rebuild. We'll note compatibility matrix in the runbook.
[09:14] Priya Nair: Great.
[09:16] Maya Chen: Let's recap what we committed to share: pricing spreadsheet update, SOC2 + network diagram, benchmark harness repo link, pilot load checklist, and a proposed pilot kickoff calendar. Any other items?
[09:29] Tom Reynolds: Please also include the SLA language exemplar.
[09:32] Maya Chen: Noted.
[09:33] Priya Nair: For the sample prompts — we'll sanitize and share by early next week.
[09:37] Maya Chen: Awesome. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and a 30-min kickoff.
[09:43] Liam Ortiz: I'll start prepping the harness and checklist; I'll also add a short runbook for troubleshooting anticipated failure modes (KV mismatch, high tail due to long seqs).
[09:55] Sara Gomez: Any rough estimate on how long VPC peering setup takes?
[09:58] Liam Ortiz: Generally a one-business-day window if CIDRs are available and teams are responsive; sometimes firewall approval takes longer. We'll provide a prescriptive checklist to expedite.
[10:10] Maya Chen: OK, unless there's anything else we'll wrap. Thank you all for your time.
[10:15] Priya Nair: Thanks.
[10:16] Tom Reynolds: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:17] Sara Gomez: Bye.
